question_text: A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician because of intermittent episodes of sharp chest pain and palpitations. She appears nervous. Her pulse is 115/min and irregularly irregular, and blood pressure is 139/86 mmHg. Examination shows a fine tremor on both hands and digital swelling; the extremities are warm. There is retraction of the right upper eyelid. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?

                    ### Question
                    A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician because of intermittent episodes of sharp chest pain and palpitations. She appears nervous. Her pulse is 115/min and irregularly irregular, and blood pressure is 139/86 mmHg. Examination shows a fine tremor on both hands and digital swelling; the extremities are warm. There is retraction of the right upper eyelid. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Amiodarone
opb. Propylthiouracil
opc. Warfarin
opd. Methimazole
ope. Propranolol

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient likely has hyperthyroidism presenting with symptoms of chest pain, palpitations, tachycardia, and irregular pulse. Given the classic signs of hyperthyroidism like fine tremor, digital swelling, warm extremities, and retraction of the right upper eyelid, the next step should involve addressing the underlying thyroid dysfunction. Beta-blockers such as propranolol are indicated for symptom control in hyperthyroidism. Antithyroid medications like propylthiouracil or methimazole may be considered to block thyroid hormone synthesis. Warfarin is not the most appropriate next step in this case.
